Technical requirements

What SATOM must do and what it needs to run, in one place — scope, core capabilities with their permission keys, supported products and builds, platform and runtime stack, sizing, network ports, security, availability, the non-functional rules and the known limits.

This page is the one-stop reference for a new engineer or an evaluating customer: what SATOM is for, what it does, and what a node needs to run it. It summarises and links; the linked articles hold the detail. Everything here describes release 4.12.0.

Purpose and scope#

SATOM (System Automation & Task Orchestration Manager) is a web console that administers a fleet of Fortinet appliances over their own management interfaces — REST first, SSH/CLI only where the API cannot reach. It is built as a Flask application with PostgreSQL behind it.

SATOM is:

  • a central place to read, change, back up and upgrade appliances, with a preview before every write and an audit row after it;
  • DB-first: pages read a local cache of each device's configuration, so the console stays usable when an appliance is slow, unreachable or licence-locked. Going live to the device is an explicit action;
  • an automation layer (jobs, scheduled actions, change requests, processes) and a monitoring layer (metrics, probes, alerting) over the same inventory.

SATOM is not:

  • a replacement for the appliances: they keep working without it, and the device stays the source of truth for its configuration;
  • a vendor-site crawler: release notes, upgrade paths and API knowledge for builds you do not run arrive as signed packs (API library);
  • a generic configuration-write API: its own integration API is deliberately narrow (API).

For the architecture behind this, read Architecture and System overview.

Core capabilities#

The permission keys are the granular keys of a profile; see Users and profiles and Permissions.

Functional area Capability Main permission key(s) Article
Devices and lifecycle Inventory, rediscovery, health, configuration backups and restore, firmware upgrade runbooks, provisioning appliances.view, appliances.edit, appliances.apply, backups.view, backups.create, backups.restore, operations.apply appliances, rediscovery, backups, firmware-upgrade, provisioning
FortiWeb policies Server policies, server objects, web protection profiles, exceptions and signatures, templates and fleet objects protection.view, protection.edit, protection.apply, network.view, network.edit, network.apply, operations.template_save, operations.template_apply, operations.template_approve server-policy, server-objects, web-protection, exceptions, template-library
Other products FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator and FortiGate workspaces; the Web Server Manager of the Linux ADOM network.view, network.edit, registry.view, registry.execute_write, webserver.view fortiadc, fortianalyzer, fortiauthenticator, fortigate, web-server-manager
Monitoring Fleet dashboards, metrics collection and the metrics store, probes, alerting, search, reports monitoring.view monitoring-overview, metrics, probes, alerting
Automation and change control Background jobs, scheduled actions, change requests, processes, locks operations.view, operations.apply, operations.scripts_run jobs, scheduled-actions, change-requests, process, locks
Tools, Scout, Plugin Studio Troubleshooting tools, Scout (AI assistant), Plugin Studio apps, Script Library, Python Console, Lua Studio advisor.use, <a class="dc-perm" href="permissions.html#monitoring-probe_free" title="Probe free targets — Point the certificate inspector and the transaction tracer at a
host SATOM does not manage. Inventory destinations never need this.">monitoring.probe_free, studio.plugin_studio, studio.script_library, studio.python_console, studio.lua_studio tools-menu, scout, plugin-studio-start, script-library
Administration Users and profiles, settings, audit log, node certificates, system backup, software update, high availability users.manage, profiles.manage, audit.view users-and-profiles, settings, audit-log, system-backup, software-update, high-availability
API Token-authenticated integration API at /api/v1; the Fortinet endpoint registry and API explorer users.manage (tokens), registry.view, registry.edit, registry.execute_write api, api-tokens, api-registry

Three system profiles ship: readonly (every read key), operator (reads plus the day-to-day write keys) and admin (every key). Keys marked admin-only in app/permissions.py, such as users.manage and operations.template_approve, are not in the operator profile.

Supported products and firmware#

Product ADOM Channel
FortiWeb /web/ REST, plus SSH/CLI for troubleshooting reads and certificate key upload
FortiADC /adc/ REST
FortiAuthenticator /fac/ REST (API key); SSH with its own credential when needed
FortiAnalyzer /faz/ JSON-RPC
FortiGate /fgt/ REST, read live; edits limited to cmdb objects, dry run first

Support is decided per exact build, never per API version or firmware line (Build compatibility). Before a template, profile, baseline or carve-out is written, SATOM checks every field against the target build and skips, warns or blocks per appliance.

The signed API pack shipped with 4.12.0 carries measured endpoint baselines for these builds:

Product Builds with a measured baseline
FortiWeb 7.6.8, 8.0.5, 8.0.6
FortiADC 7.6.7, 8.0.3, 8.0.4
FortiAnalyzer 7.6.7
FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3
FortiGate 8.0.1, 8.0.2

For a build outside this list, fields with no evidence read unknown and are reported as "cannot be guaranteed", never as ok. A template apply to a build with no evidence at all is blocked by the template's firmware check. Newer knowledge packs and rediscovery of a real appliance fill the gaps.

Platform requirements#

Operating system and install shapes#

Shape Supported targets Notes
Native, online Debian 12 (reference), RHEL/Rocky/Alma 9, openSUSE Leap 15 / SLES 15, Arch install-satom.sh; needs HTTPS egress to the distribution mirrors, PyPI and the code repository
Native, offline bundle Debian 12, RHEL/Rocky/Alma 9, openSUSE Leap 15 / SLES 15 One bundle per distribution family; no Internet egress. Arch has no offline bundle
Guided Debian 12/13, Ubuntu 22.04/24.04, RHEL/Rocky/Alma 9, openSUSE Leap/SLES 15 satom-setup.sh checks the machine, then runs the native or Docker install
Docker A container host One stack: application, PostgreSQL, Redis, metrics store and an nginx proxy

Every native install needs systemd as PID 1 (Alpine/musl is not supported), amd64/x86_64, and an account with sudo scoped to the installer for the install window. Run sudo bash install-satom.sh --preflight to check a machine without changing it. Full procedure: Installation.

Runtime stack#

Component Native install Docker stack
Python ≥ 3.10 in its own venv (python3.11 on EL9 and SUSE) 3.11
Flask / Werkzeug Flask 3.1.3, Werkzeug 3.1.9 (pinned in requirements.txt) same image
SQLAlchemy / psycopg SQLAlchemy 2.1.5, psycopg 3.3.6 same image
Application server gunicorn 26.2.0: 4 workers × 8 threads, bound to 127.0.0.1:8000 same
Database the distribution's PostgreSQL package PostgreSQL 15 (or an existing external server)
Metrics store VictoriaMetrics 1.148.0 (single node, sha256-verified), 127.0.0.1:8428, 396-day retention VictoriaMetrics 1.148.0
Reverse proxy / TLS the distribution's nginx nginx 1.27
Rate-limit storage in-process (memory://) unless RATELIMIT_STORAGE_URI points at Redis Redis 7
Sandbox bubblewrap — the code tools refuse to run without it in the image

The installer also installs rsync, openssl, ca-certificates, curl, sudo and git (online), and openssh in cluster mode only. It compiles nothing and uses only the distribution's official repositories.

Browser#

The console needs a current browser and no Internet access from it: every script, stylesheet and font (Bootstrap, Bootstrap Icons, Chart.js) is vendored and served by the node, and the Content-Security-Policy names no other origin.

Sizing#

The installer's floor is 2 vCPU, 2 GB RAM, 15 GB disk. That is what the installer needs to finish, not a recommendation. Size for the fleet:

Tier Devices Policies per device vCPU RAM Disk
Lab / PoC ≤ 10 ≤ 100 2 4 GB 20 GB
Small ≤ 25 ≤ 250 4 4 GB 30 GB
Medium ≤ 60 ≤ 250 4 8 GB 40 GB
Large ≤ 110 ≤ 750 8 8 GB 120 GB
  • The binding constraint is device I/O inside the 3-minute collection window. Past about 110 devices, split the fleet across independent installations instead of growing the node.
  • Disk grows with devices × policies, not with device count alone.
  • Keep max(15 % of the volume, 3 GB) free. PostgreSQL stops when it cannot write a checkpoint, and /healthz keeps answering 200 while it does. Watch free space from outside the node.

Details and the formulas: Installation — Sizing.

Network requirements#

Port Direction Purpose Required
Console port (default 443/tcp) browser → node HTTPS web console and /api/v1 always
80/tcp browser (and a public ACME CA) → node redirect to HTTPS; /.well-known/acme-challenge/ always (fixed port)
Appliance port (default 443/tcp, per device) node → appliance management REST / JSON-RPC always
Appliance SSH (default 22/tcp, per device) node → appliance CLI reads, certificate key upload, CLI writer where used
8443/tcp node ↔ node health and status probes: TLS plus HMAC-signed requests cluster only (fixed port)
5432/tcp standby → primary PostgreSQL streaming replication, TLS with verify-ca cluster only
22/tcp standby → primary rsync of data/ over SSH, read-only, restricted key cluster only
HTTPS egress node → Internet install (mirrors, PyPI, repository), update feed, knowledge feed, PyPI for library updates online mode only

gunicorn (127.0.0.1:8000) and the metrics store (127.0.0.1:8428) listen on loopback only. Optional outbound connections follow your settings: directory servers (Authentication), the mail server for alerts and external AI providers for Scout.

ℹ️Note — Isolated networks

A node with no Internet egress installs from an offline bundle and updates from a signed offline update package uploaded through Software Update. Knowledge packs are uploaded the same way. See Offline updates.

Both cluster nodes must be NTP-synchronised. A peer request whose signature timestamp is more than 120 seconds off is refused.

Security requirements#

Area Requirement as shipped
Transport nginx terminates TLS 1.2/1.3; plain HTTP answers 301 to HTTPS. The install issues a certificate from a per-node internal CA; replace it with your own or use ACME (Node TLS)
Appliance TLS Verified by default against the trust store; turned off only per device, explicitly (Trust store)
Authentication Local accounts (scrypt), optional TOTP 2FA, LDAP/AD/RADIUS. 10 consecutive failures lock an account for 15 minutes. Passwords are 12–1024 characters
Authorisation RBAC on the route, not only in the template: a missing key returns 403
Session Cookie Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax; idle session lock (default 60 minutes)
Browser headers Nonce-based CSP with script-src-attr 'none' (no inline handlers), HSTS, X-Frame-Options: DENY (same-origin frames only where SATOM embeds itself), nosniff, CSRF tokens on every form
Secrets Appliance credentials Fernet-encrypted in the database; SECRET_KEY, FERNET_KEY and the DB password only in the environment file (root:satom 0640). Losing FERNET_KEY loses every stored credential: back it up
Privilege The application runs as an unprivileged, shell-less service account. Its sudo allowlist is nginx -t and systemctl reload nginx. Privileged work goes through one root runner (satom-updater.service) that validates its input
Code tools Operator-supplied Python (Script Library runs, integration hooks, the Python Console) runs in a bubblewrap jail with no access to the application tree or the database socket
Audit Every write snapshots first, writes an audit row and records the before and after state (Audit log)

Read Security model for the full model and Safeguards for every guard, with how to verify it is armed.

Availability#

Production can run as a primary/standby pair (High availability):

What How it reaches the standby
Database (settings, users, devices, everything in PostgreSQL) PostgreSQL streaming replication, continuous
Files under data/ (bundles, configuration vault, source-of-truth store) the standby pulls them with rsync over SSH every 5 minutes
Application code Software Update on each node, standby first
Metrics store not replicated: each node keeps its own
  • The standby's scheduler stays on hold, so two nodes never fire the same scheduled action.
  • Failover is manual. An administrator promotes the standby from the High Availability page, confirming the node's hostname.
  • The standby protects against the loss of the primary. It does not add capacity. To manage more devices, split the fleet (Sizing).

A single node is protected by the nightly system backup (System backup).

Non-functional rules#

These are the product rules every feature is held to (Product rules):

writes

Six-step device writes

Pre-check, versioned backup, dry-run diff, minimal change in dependency order, post-check by re-reading the object, compensation or restore. A second run makes zero changes.

correctness

HTTP 200 is not success

SATOM reads the response body. A licence error or rejected read returned with a 200 is shown as ERROR, never as empty or ok.

load

Cache first, device last

Browsing reads the stored cache. Reaching the appliance is an explicit job that the operator can see.

completeness

Every field is visible

Fields the vendor GUI hides appear under Not in GUI, but in CLI with their channel (Not in GUI).

look

Light UI only

There is no dark mode. Only the navigation chrome and code blocks are dark (Design system).

language

English is the source language

Everything shipped is written in English. The console offers German, Spanish, French and Italian translations (Languages).

Out of scope and known limits#

  • Container installs disable five host-only actions: Software Update, HA promotion, service control, certificate activation and systemd unit health. The optional operations agent brings back four of them. HA promotion stays a manual PostgreSQL procedure.
  • No automatic failover between SATOM nodes.
  • One node collects about 110 devices in its 3-minute window. Larger fleets need several independent installations.
  • The integration API cannot upgrade, flash or reboot an appliance, run an action flagged destructive, or write arbitrary configuration.
  • Template rollout targets FortiWeb appliances only (template_apply.SUPPORTED_KINDS).
  • The FortiGate API console writes to /api/v2/cmdb/ only, and is dry-run by default.
  • Alpine/musl is not supported, and Arch has no offline bundle.
  • The node serves no manual. The published copy is this site. On an isolated node, read the bundled manuals with satom show docs.
  • /healthz answering 200 does not prove the database is healthy. Monitor disk space and PostgreSQL from outside the node.
